entities.summary: Nicolò de' Tudeschi (Panormitanus) was a prominent Italian Benedictine canonist who played a crucial role in shaping the medieval legal landscape. Born in the 14th century, Panormitanus spent most of his life in the service of the Holy See, where he worked tirelessly to codify and disseminate the principles of canon law. His magnum opus, 'De antiquis iure' (On Ancient Law), became a seminal work in the field, influencing generations of scholars and jurists. Panormitanus's work not only helped establish the Catholic Church as a major player in European politics but also laid the groundwork for the development of modern civil law systems. In the centuries that followed, his ideas continued to shape the jurisprudence of European monarchies, contributing to the growth of a unified legal framework across the continent. As a result, Panormitanus's legacy serves as a testament to the enduring power of medieval scholarship and the far-reaching impact of the Catholic Church on Western civilization.
